rrw_boatman.text: The steamship has been sailing since 1900. I keep telling it to retire and it keeps coming in on time.
Glasgow drinks this loch. Every time a Glaswegian pours a glass of water, a Trossachs sheep gets a bit more famous.

rrw_minister.text: Rob Roy is buried here with his wife and two of his sons. The stone is plain. He would have approved: he did not like a fuss, unless it was the other side's.
There is a very good tearoom down the road. I would put it on the list ahead of the grave, to be honest.

rrw_film.text: They shot a silly film about a grail here. A very silly film. The coconuts were not the castle's idea.
It is a fine castle. It has been in more films than I have, and it has not once asked for a better trailer.

rrw_walker.text: Drymen to Pitlochry on foot. I am doing it in my own time, which is a polite way of saying I stop for tea.
Fàilte to the Trossachs. That is 'welcome'. Walter Scott gave the place a reputation. It has been living off it since.

rrw_osprey.text: An osprey hangs over the water, then drops like a dropped umbrella and comes up with lunch. It looks at you as if you had not seen anything.
